transcript.text: HELP theres flames inside my microwave, a bag of popcorn caught fire, what do i do??

⚠ Stop using this appliance
If there are flames or smoke is still coming from it, keep away, don't open the door of an oven, microwave or dryer that is on fire, switch it off at the wall or the fuse box only if you can do that safely, get everyone out and call 999.
door is closed. i switched it off at the wall, flames went out after a minute but theres loads of smoke inside and the alarm is going off. flatmate is here. should i call 999?

⚠ Stop using this appliance
A burning or hot-plastic smell, smoke, scorching or melting can mean an electrical fault or a fire risk. Stop using it, switch it off and unplug it (or turn it off at the fuse box), and don't run it again — not even as a test — until it has been checked by a qualified engineer. If the flames are fully out, it's switched off at the wall and the door is shut, you don't have to call 999. But if you're unsure at any point, call 999 anyway. The fire service would much rather come out for nothing. 1. Opening it now just lets the smoke out and feeds air in.
2. Open windows and doors to the outside to clear the room, and fan the smoke alarm rather than disabling it.
3. Stay nearby but not right next to it, and keep watching it for 20 to 30 minutes.
4. Don't use it again until it's been checked. A fire inside a microwave can damage the cavity coating and the small cover over the microwave outlet (the waveguide cover), and it can damage the internals. Microwaves hold dangerous voltages inside even when unplugged, so that's not something to open up yourself. With a cheaper microwave, replacing it is often the sensible choice. When things have settled, what make and model is it? It's usually on a label inside the door frame or on the back. I can then tell you what's worth checking and whether there's any safety notice to look out for.
